title: Admission pipeline: convert community LLM weights to runtime artifacts, pin versions, and publish perf profiles
creator: Amira Patel
description: Build an end-to-end admission pipeline that takes community model weights (HF tarballs and custom checkpoints), runs a deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime artifacts, performs automated validation and microbench profiling, pins a canonical model version, and publishes a verified performance profile to the model catalog. This ticket scopes the engineering work to implement the conversion flow, validation checks, publish hooks, and the version pinning metadata model. The goal is to reduce manual steps in onboarding ad-hoc community models and ensure each published model has reproducible performance characteristics and a rollback-safe pinning strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline accepts HF/torch checkpoints and produces a runtime artifact (quantized when applicable) with artifacts stored in GCS and a content-hash-based version ID
Automated validation runs: sanity generation tests, token-accurate KV cache handling, and end-to-end latency/throughput microbenchmarks for configured seq lengths
A model version is pinned in the catalog with metadata: source-hash, conversion-recipe-id, quantization-profile, kernel-hints, and perf-profile link
Performance profiles are published to the catalog UI and available via API with metrics: p50/p90 latency per batch size, tokens/sec, memory footprint, and max-seqlen SLO
Conversion errors produce actionable logs and an automated triage tag; failed admissions are quarantined with a link to failure artifacts
Canary ingestion of 5 community models completed without manual intervention and with guardrails in place (quota limits, runtime sandboxing)
implementation_notes: Use an isolated 'admission' k8s job with a nonce'd sandbox namespace to mount incoming weight blobs
Leverage existing weight-conversion service (rw-weights-bridge) and add a deterministic conversion mode that emits content-hash and recipe file
Introduce a lightweight validation harness that runs: example prompts, kv-cache integrity check, and a short perf run (seq32/seq512) using CI GPU quota
Store artifacts in GCS under /models/admitted/{model_key}/{version}/ with metadata.json containing pin info
Publish perf profiles to the catalog via the model-catalog service with a new 'verified_profile' flag to distinguish automated vs manual entries
Pinning semantics: pin a conversion-immutable version id (content-hash), not the original HF tag; store mapping from canonical pin to upstream origin for auditability
Fallback policy: if a newer conversion fails, traffic remains pointed at last-known-good pinned version until manual or automated roll-forward passes staged validations
testing_plan: Unit tests for conversion deterministic output (hash stable across runs)
Integration tests: admission job runs on PR with synthetic weights (small toy model) and uploads artifacts to test bucket
E2E smoke: deploy converted artifact to nightly-serving cluster and run end-to-end prompt fidelity checks
Load test: run microbench harness to capture p50/p90 at multiple batch sizes under constrained GPU memory
Chaos: simulate conversion timeouts and storage failures to validate quarantine logic and observability alerts
rollback_plan: If published perf profile or pinned version causes regressions in production routing, the console can toggle 'use_verified_profile' to false for the model, which reverts routing to the previous pin
Archive problematic conversion artifacts under /models/quarantine/ with owner notifications and automatic garbage-collection after 30d
Automated re-run on a separate conversion recipe (older quantization path) if primary recipe fails more than 3 times in 24h
